doc.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-10-07

title: Playing across the street and drinking on the job
summary: De De recalls staying on while Billie joined the Filipino band, and the drinking on the bandstand.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: And what did you do today?
Where'd you go, Billy? Right across the street.
The Filipina band, right across the street.
Of course, we were the Filipina band. I was Filipina.
Right across the street. I was right there. And what'd you do today? I stayed on. They had another piano playing? I had another piano playing. I kept it full of whiskey till it couldn't work.
He tricked him. He tricked him.

Oh, McGee. No, McGee. He sent another fella just as bad. What is Joe? I can't call that boy. Joe, what is his name, Joe? Joe something, I don't know. I kept both of them. That's right. They love their liquor. I love mine, but I laid off it.
He didn't let it out and give it to them.

He could give whiskey like water. All the days giving all the drinks at night, seven, eight, ten if we wanted at the bar, we had to go and get it. And when they drink. Excuse them what the people would treat. People come in and bring you. Give you. Because they're not going to treat you. So I just poured it in them. It couldn't work. That's what it was today. That's the way of doing it, you know.
It worked me a lot though. It's my heart, you see, because it wasn't even working. I had to hold my hand up, you know.
I had to hold my hand up.
